source.title: Nanbeige4-3B Technical Report: Exploring the Frontier of Small Language Models
source.authors: Chen Yang; Guangyue Peng; Jiaying Zhu; Ran Le; Ruixiang Feng; Tao Zhang; Wei Ruan; Xiaoqi Liu; Xiaoxue Cheng; Xiyun Xu; Yang Song; Yanzipeng Gao; Yiming Jia; Yun Xing; Yuntao Wen; Zekai Wang; Zhenwei An; Zhicong Sun; Zongchao Chen

record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream benchmark performance as the cold-start SFT instruction-set size increases, but does not fit pretraining loss scaling laws.
record.gate_note: Figure 3 reports AIME 2025 and GPQA-Diamond results while scaling cold-start SFT instructions from 0.5M to 35M. The paper says performance improves substantially without clear early saturation, controlling for data distribution and quality. This bears on downstream performance with training scale (V6), but it is not a held-out pretraining-loss measurement or a power-law fit. The FG-WSD scheduler comparison and model benchmark comparisons do not test the versions’ loss-scaling or prediction claims.
record.test_reason: This is a model technical report. Its only scaling-style result (Figure 3) plots AIME 2025 and GPQA-Diamond for one 3B model against cold-start SFT instruction count (0.5M–35M). The text says only that gains continue 'without a clear early saturation point'. No loss is measured, no functional form is fitted, nothing is predicted, and pretraining scale is not varied. So it does not bear on V6's predictability from pretraining scale or loss, nor on V5's power-law form for fine-tuning. The abstract's 'scaling law' wording is rhetorical, not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Incomplete. The authors' main conclusion is that Nanbeige4-3B, trained on 23T curated tokens with FG-WSD, large-scale SFT, DPD distillation and multi-stage RL, outperforms Qwen3-8B/14B and rivals much larger models on reasoning, tool-use and alignment benchmarks. The SFT-scaling observation is a secondary motivation for their recipe.
record.recipe_differences: Scales the number of cold-start SFT instructions and measures downstream benchmark scores; it does not use the original held-out pretraining-loss scaling-law measurement or fit a compute-optimal allocation.

fits_no_version.finding: For Nanbeige4-3B, AIME 2025 and GPQA-Diamond scores keep rising as cold-start SFT instructions grow from 0.5M to 35M, with data distribution and quality held constant. No saturation is reported and no curve is fitted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream reasoning-benchmark accuracy of a small model keeps increasing with SFT instruction-set size up to tens of millions of examples.

record.problems: The instruction-scaling values are presented in Figure 3 without numerical values in the text; no uncertainty estimates are stated, and the report does not fit or test a predictive scaling function.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No small-run fits extrapolated to larger runs.
No shape ablation at fixed parameter count.
No power-law loss fit for fine-tuning, repeated data (the 6.5T upsampled tokens are not analysed) or other modalities.
No downstream predictability from pretraining scale or loss. SFT-count scaling is qualitative only and unfitted.

record.verdict_notes: Table 4 (a 3B base beating Qwen3-8B-Base after identical SFT) compares models with different pretraining data and recipes. It is not a controlled parameter-scaling test. Table 2 (FG-WSD vs WSD at 1B/1T) is the study's own method compared against a baseline. The reader's 'tests/T2' and V6 'supports' label are not justified.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameter count, tokens, or compute; power-law form and orders of magnitude.
No small-run loss fits or predictions of substantially larger runs.
No compute-budget sweep or loss-minimising parameter/token allocation.
No controlled comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No test of whether a power-law loss form holds across modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.

Tests downstream benchmark changes with cold-start SFT instruction count, not predictability from pretraining loss or parameter count, nor a fitted predictive relationship across other tasks or settings.
No analysis of loss-law exponents, compute-optimal fits, or their dependence on fitting choices or setup.

rows.subject: Nanbeige4-3B

rows.note: The text reports substantial improvement as the instruction set scales, without a clear early saturation point; the plotted numeric values are not stated in the text.
